ai.title: Convert base2 agent arrow functions to declarations
ai.summary: Refactors `createBase2` and prompt builders in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` from arrow function assignments to function declarations. This internal change standardizes code style for the base2 agent definition logic. No user-facing behavior or API changes occur.

eli5.text: The assistant team cleaned up how the base2 agent's instructions are written behind the scenes, switching from one coding style to a more standard one. This is purely an internal cleanup with no change to what the assistant does or how fast it responds. If you looked at the code, you'd see the way prompts are organized now matches the team's preferred pattern, but as a user you wouldn't notice any difference in behavior.

ai.title: Refactor best-of-n orchestrator to factory pattern
ai.summary: Replaces static best-of-n-orchestrator-fast and best-of-n-orchestrator-gpt-5 definitions with a createBestOfNOrchestrator factory function in best-of-n-orchestrator.ts. The factory accepts 'sonnet' or 'gpt-5' model identifiers, dynamically assigning models, display names, spawnable agents, and handleSteps generators. Updates base2.ts to reference the unified 'best-of-n-orchestrator' ID, removing the fast variant branch. This consolidation eliminates code duplication while preserving distinct GPT-5 and Sonnet orchestration behaviors.

eli5.text: If you use the coding assistant in its internal testing mode, the program that coordinates multiple helper agents to write code has been simplified. Instead of maintaining two nearly identical coordinator programs that differed only by which AI model they used, they now share one coordinator that picks the right model automatically. The only visible effect is that the internal name used to reference the non-GPT-5 coordinator changed from 'best-of-n-orchestrator-fast' to 'best-of-n-orchestrator'; everything else you'd experience stays the same. The old coordinator program file was removed, but the GPT-5 version still exists and simply calls the shared coordinator internally.

ai.title: Remove file-researcher from base2 agent
ai.summary: Removed `file-researcher` from `spawnableAgents` and deleted conditional prompt instructions in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`. Unified context-gathering guidance to rely on `file-picker-max`, `code-searcher`, and other agents without GPT-5 branching. Internal refactor of agent orchestration logic.

eli5.text: The agent no longer delegates initial file research to a specialized helper; instead, it uses a different file-finding tool alongside its existing search and directory tools, and it skips the conditional instructions for older model versions. Users will not notice a change in behavior for this specific refactor, since the agent still completes the same steps but through a streamlined path. This is live today as internal housekeeping that simplifies how the agent gathers initial context.

ai.title: Add n param to best-of-n orchestrator
ai.summary: The `best-of-n-orchestrator` agents now accept an optional `n` input parameter to control the number of parallel implementor agents spawned. Previously hardcoded to 5, the orchestrator now uses `params.n` (defaulting to 5, clamped between 1 and 10) to dynamically generate the agent list for both GPT-5 and Sonnet variants. This change applies to `.agents/base2/best-of-n/best-of-n-orchestrator.ts` and updates prompt guidelines in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to reflect the new capability for tuning proposal counts based on task complexity.

eli5.text: When the assistant team works on a task, it can spawn multiple helper agents to each try solving the problem in parallel, then pick the best result, like asking several people to write the same report and choosing the best one. Previously, it always spawned exactly five helpers no matter the task. Now, whoever is directing the work can specify how many helpers to use, with the number automatically kept between 1 and 10. You wouldn't notice this directly, but if you were giving instructions on a very simple or very complex task, the team coordinating the helpers now has flexibility to adjust how many people they ask to pitch in, rather than always defaulting to five.

ai.title: Rename best-of-n-orchestrator to best-of-n-editor
ai.summary: Renamed the agent definition, file, and function from best-of-n-orchestrator to best-of-n-editor. Updated references in base2.ts and base2-gpt-5-worker.ts to use the new id and gpt-5 variant. No functional change to the orchestration logic itself.

eli5.text: A background assistant that drafts code changes has been renamed from "orchestrator" to "editor", which better reflects its role of editing code by testing multiple options and applying the best one. The underlying process remains the same, but the updated name and slightly adjusted instructions make it clearer how it should be used when making code improvements.

ai.title: Add readsubtree tool
ai.summary: New read_subtree tool added to agent runtime and common constants. Reads directory subtrees or file variables, returning a truncated blob based on maxTokens. Registered in tool lists, definitions, handlers, and UI renderers across core, CLI, and agent packages. Defaults to 4000 token budget, truncating by dropping variables then deepest files.

eli5.text: The AI assistant you interact with can now pull back a quick snapshot of the project's folder structure along with the key variables defined inside your files, all in one response. When you (or the assistant) ask it to review where things live in your project, it will hand back a condensed view that covers directories, file names, and parsed variables, and if that view gets too large it will trim the deepest files and drop file variables first until it fits a default size limit of roughly 4000 tokens. You would notice this as a faster, more focused answer about your project layout instead of a long, unfiltered dump of every directory and file.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to show its environment settings, the list now displays correctly whether you're running the program from source or using a pre-built executable. Previously, the display only worked in development mode and could appear empty or broken in the packaged executable; now it reads from a single source of truth that works in both modes. Additionally, any environment value longer than 50 characters is automatically shortened and ends with an ellipsis, so the settings panel no longer overflows with very long text.

eli5.text: The software kit now exposes a definition for how files are organized and accessed, so other tools that build on it can reference that structure directly. This affects developers who pull in the kit to extend or integrate with the platform, letting them work with file-system concepts without guessing the expected shape. Nothing visible changes for end users today, but it removes a hurdle that previously forced integrators to rely on internal details.

ai.title: Bump SDK version to 0.5.12
ai.summary: The SDK package version advanced from 0.5.11 to 0.5.12 in this release-bump commit, capturing the accumulated user-visible work since 0.0.3 across the preceding days. The single diff hunk in sdk/package.json touches only the version string; all substantive changes shipped within this release are described by the release notes rather than by source modifications in this commit. Notable additions in 0.5.12 include GPT-5 orchestration support in the base2 agent, the read_subtree tool, task_completed turn termination, and code-search JSON streaming with early stop.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json: version field changed from 0.5.11 to 0.5.12; no other files modified in diff

eli5.text: This release brings GPT-5 support to the agent system, plus new tools for ending tasks explicitly and searching code safely. The upgrade adds GPT-5 model support to the coding agent, enables a new 'task completed' tool that lets agents signal they are done working instead of guessing, and improves code search with better timeouts and JSON-based parsing that handles special characters in filenames. The code search now includes surrounding context lines alongside matches and prevents hangs on slow searches, while best-of-n agents now support a configurable number of parallel options (1 to 10) instead of a fixed count. Upgrading gives you access to the latest GPT-5 reasoning model for complex coding tasks, more reliable and faster code searches that won't freeze your terminal, explicit task-completion control to reduce guesswork, and the ability to tune how many solution proposals the system explores for each problem.

eli5.text: If your analytics tool wasn't turned on yet, the system now turns it on automatically before sending any usage data, instead of just throwing the data away. This means your product usage still gets tracked even when things start up in a different order. You won't see a difference directly, but behind the scenes, your activity data is being captured more reliably.

ai.title: Handlesteps run outside QuickJS sandbox
ai.summary: Programmatic handlesteps generators now execute via native `eval` instead of QuickJS. Removes `SandboxManager` dependency from `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`. String-based templates compile to native generators; `clearAgentGeneratorCache` drops sandbox disposal logic. Scope limited to agent runtime step execution.

eli5.text: When a programmatic handlestep generator is an inline string of code, it now runs directly in the agent runtime instead of inside a separate QuickJS sandbox. You would notice this if you were tracing execution: the handlestep code executes in the main runtime context with native `eval` rather than being sandboxed. This removes the QuickJS sandboxing layer from the agent runtime's step execution path, so any handlestep logic that previously ran in isolation now runs alongside the main agent code. The change affects handlestep execution in the agent runtime and is live today.

ai.title: Add logger param to clearAgentGeneratorCache
ai.summary: clearAgentGeneratorCache in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-programmatic-step.ts now requires a params object containing a logger. This aligns the test helper with the Logger dependency pattern used elsewhere in the agent runtime. Internal change only; no user-facing behavior impact.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes testing tool used by developers building AI assistants now asks for a logging helper upfront instead of grabbing one on its own when clearing its temporary memory between practice runs. This is purely internal housekeeping, the change affects only the code that resets test state, not anything you would see or do. Developers running tests of the assistant runtime may notice the helper now expects a logger object passed in, but the end result of clearing that temporary memory stays exactly the same. This is a minor adjustment that aligns the testing setup with the logging approach used elsewhere in the assistant runtime.

Previously, the welcome message included lines showing each setting name and its value, truncated if very long. Now those lines are gone, so the startup output contains fewer details, but the assistant itself works the same way once you start typing.

Modified agent-run and chat-completion API handlers in `web` to inject user context (id, email, discord_id) into logs via the new helper. This ensures structured logging captures relevant user metadata for debugging API interactions.

eli5.text: The system now captures more details about who is making each API request (your email and Discord ID) alongside its internal logs, so the debugging information includes identifying context for the agent-run and chat-completion endpoints. This affects anyone sending traffic to those API routes, and you'd notice it only if you were inspecting the structured logs, where user metadata now appear attached to each log entry. It is live today as part of the merged changes across those routes.

ai.summary: Adds missing `loggerWithContext` mock to agent-runs and chat-completions unit tests. Resolves typecheck errors caused by new `LoggerWithContextFn` requirement. Internal test infrastructure only.

eli5.text: The team updated their internal testing setup so automated tests can run again after a recent behind-the-scenes change that required a new logging component. Think of it like adding a missing prop to a few puppet shows so the puppets don't break mid-performance. This only affects the engineers' tools; you won't see any difference in the app today. It's live in their codebase but only impacts how they build and test new features.

ai.title: Extract handleSlashCommands router and define AgentMode type
ai.summary: Extracted slash command routing logic into `cli/src/utils/slash-commands.ts` with a new `handleSlashCommands` function, reducing inline complexity in `cli/src/chat.tsx`. Introduced `AgentMode` type in `cli/src/utils/constants.ts` to replace hardcoded `'FAST' | 'MAX'` unions across `cli/src/state/chat-store.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`, and `cli/src/components/agent-mode-toggle.tsx`. Scope limited to CLI core utilities and state management; no external API or model changes. `handleSlashCommands` accepts explicit refs and setters for `agentMode`, `inputValue`, and `logoutMutation` to decouple UI state from command execution.

eli5.text: A small behind-the-scenes cleanup in the command-line program made its internal code easier to follow and less error-prone, but it doesn't add any new features or change how the program behaves today. The team pulled the slash-commands (the /help, /login and similar shortcuts you type in) out of the main file and gave them their own home, and they also gave the two operating styles ('Fast' and 'Max') a single shared label so every part of the program agrees on what those names mean. You won't notice anything different while chatting, but the program is a bit tidier under the hood.

ai.title: Add /init command to CLI slash-command handlers
ai.summary: New /init command registered in cli/src/slash-commands/handlers.ts and implemented in cli/src/slash-commands/init.ts. Core types (ChatMessage, ContentBlock, ChatTheme) moved from chat.tsx and utils/theme-system.ts to cli/src/types/, requiring import path updates across chat.tsx and components like agent-mode-toggle.tsx, branch-item.tsx, login-modal.tsx, message-block.tsx, separator.tsx, status-indicator.tsx, suggestion-menu.tsx, use-message-renderer.tsx, and use-send-message.ts. useSendMessage now returns a typed SendMessageFn from cli/src/types/contracts/send-message.ts.

eli5.text: You can now type /init in the chat to kick off a new session setup, similar to how you might type a command to create a file or run a search. This new command is wired into the existing set of slash commands you already use, so it behaves just like them, you enter it, hit enter, and the assistant starts whatever /init is programmed to do. The change also quietly reorganized some shared definitions into a common library that several parts of the app now reference, which is why files like message-block.tsx, branch-item.tsx, and login-modal.tsx show up in the change. It's live today, so if you open a fresh session, /init is available right away.

ai.title: Remove mergeTextSegments heuristic from CLI stream handler
ai.summary: Deleted mergeTextSegments in cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts. Stream chunks now append directly to accumulators. Fixes rendering issues caused by overlap detection. Scope limited to CLI text streaming.

eli5.text: When you chat with an assistant in the command line, the words appear on your screen piece by piece as they arrive. This change removes a background helper that tried to guess which pieces overlapped with what had already been shown, and instead just appends each new piece in order. You wouldn't see the words typed differently, but you should see fewer cases where parts of the answer pop up twice or get cut off during the live preview while the assistant is still typing.

ai.title: Rename slash-commands to commands, handleSlashCommands
ai.summary: CLI internal refactor renames slash-commands directory to commands and handleSlashCommands function to routeUserPrompt. Files moved: cli/src/slash-commands/init.ts to cli/src/commands/init.ts, cli/src/slash-commands/handlers.ts to cli/src/commands/router.ts. Import updated in cli/src/chat.tsx. ai.title: Inline store agent data fetch
ai.summary: Store page fetches agent data directly via `getCachedAgents` instead of self-fetching `/api/agents`. Changes affect `web/src/app/store/agents-data.ts` and introduce `web/src/server/agents-data.ts` for shared logic. Build-time errors are suppressed in CI/production builds via `NEXT_PHASE` check.

eli5.text: When you visit the store's agent listing page, the site now pulls the agent data directly from its local database instead of making a separate request to its own agents API. This removes an extra network hop that could fail during the site's initial generation, so the store page loads more reliably. The shared data-fetching logic now lives in one place that both the page and the API can use, and the change is live today.
